name: Half-timbered wall
description: A straight section of half-timbered village house wall on a low fieldstone plinth: a dark weathered oak sill, corner posts, a top plate and one diagonal brace framing warm off-white lime plaster. Each section is 1.5 m long, so sections join end to end. The `_low` variant is a cutaway wall (about 1.4 m) for roofless village buildings, so what is inside stays visible. Panel variants so a run of wall is not one repeated panel: `_window` (a small lattice window), `_plain` (plaster only), `_stone` (a high fieldstone base) and `_post` (a heavy corner post, the brace the other way), each also `_low`. `_rubble` (and `_stone_rubble`, each also `_low`) build the plinth in the rubble stone of the stone walls: rounded stones of mixed sizes with dark recessed joints.

provenance.prompt: A straight section of half-timbered village house wall, 1 tile long (1.5 m) along x through the tile centre, about 0.3 m thick and 2.4 m high. A low fieldstone plinth (0.3 m), dark weathered oak sill beam, corner posts at both ends, a top plate and one diagonal brace, with warm off-white lime plaster panels between the timbers (not pure white, slightly uneven). Footprint 1x1 tile; sections join end to end. Structure, static; blocks movement and sight, cover three-quarters, not destructible.
